minutes.headline: Select Board created a budget task force, continued Blue Sky Golf's liquor hearing to July 9, extended town manager's contract
minutes.summary: The board heard public comment on a land sale, appointments and building repairs, then continued the Blue Sky Golf alcohol license hearing for missing hours and alcohol policy. It approved a pride flag request, ratified town appointments, extended existing outdoor dining arrangements and created a budget task force. After executive session it voted to extend the town manager's contract.

public_comment.topic: Invited the board to the cultural council's tray auction fundraiser to fund school arts programs as ARPA funds run out.
Asked the board to set a hearing on his 61B land sale and sign the notice for the third lot.

public_comment.stated_role: chair of the architectural preservation district commission
public_comment.topic: Urged reappointment of Richard McGrath and pressed for action on the over-budget town hall and Ritter building repairs and a job order contract.
Cemetery needs and funding, a cemetery corporation, and concern about a finance committee member serving as liaison.
Reported possible roof leaks near TV equipment, opposed creating a budget task force, and asked about the Personnel committee resignations.

votes.motion: Continue the Blue Sky Golf public hearing to 7:15 on July 9.
Approve Democratic Party Town Committee request to raise the pride flag June 23 to June 29.
Ratify appointment of Mason kefir as seasonal lifeguard.
Ratify appointment of William heslet as alternate Building Commissioner.
Ratify special police officer appointments from Shirley and Lancaster.
Appoint Richard McGrath to the architectural preservation district commission, term to 2027.
Appoint Anna Lockwood to the Council on Aging, term to June 30, 2027.
Continue existing outdoor dining arrangements until a town outdoor dining policy is adopted.
Create the budget task force as written in the charge with membership amendments.
Nominate Renee Emy as select board representative on the budget task force.
Approve town manager's payout of two remaining vacation days for FY24.
Enter executive session under c.30A s.21 para 3 for non-union contract negotiations, roll call.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call, all aye as heard)

votes.motion: Extend the 2021-2024 town manager employment agreement until August 4, 2024.

budget_items.what_was_said: Police received a state grant for a shared clinician with Lancaster, supplemented by opioid stabilization account money.
The single bid exceeded the available appropriation, so more funds would need town meeting approval to rebid.
The revised hauler proposal would exceed the appropriation, so the contract is going out to bid.
The town manager plans a process to allocate the grant services money among requesting departments.
An amount tied to the school override discussion was returned to uncommitted ARPA funds, and a Boys and Girls Club payment was in the warrant.
A member urged allocating ARPA money for a consultant on solar panels at the old dump.
The town manager estimated contractor support costs for tax billing, with discussion of a longer term contract through 2026.
Payroll and accounts payable warrants were read out.
A resident described cemetery staffing and perpetual care budget needs.

decisions.decision: Chapter 61B notice hearing to be scheduled for July 9 after town counsel review.
Blue Sky Golf to bring hours of operation and a written alcohol policy to the July 9 hearing.
Shady Point to be invited to the next meeting to discuss the boat launch license agreement; the town manager will get insurance company comments.
Select board goals for FY2025 to be discussed at the July 16 meeting.
Financial policies draft to be reviewed in chapters over time; sent to finance committee and others for feedback.
IT policy to be retitled as employee use and revised to remove the board and committee sentence; no vote taken.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to extend the 2021-2024 town manager employment agreement to August 4, 2024, after an executive session.
The board created a budget task force under a written charge with membership amendments, and nominated a Select Board representative to it.
The Blue Sky Golf alcohol and amusement license hearing was continued to July 9; the owner is to bring hours of operation and a written alcohol policy.
The board voted to keep existing outdoor dining arrangements in place until the town adopts an outdoor dining policy.
The town manager reported that the trash and recycling contract will go out to bid because the hauler's revised proposal exceeds the appropriation.

why_it_matters: The budget task force is a new body that will work on the town's budget process, and a resident who wants a say in it can follow its charge and membership.
The trash contract going to bid and the Woodruff cleanup bid exceeding its appropriation point to costs that could come before a town meeting vote.
Ownership of a liquor license, outdoor dining rules and the town manager's contract are decided by this board, not by a ballot, so the meeting record is where residents can follow them.
watch_next: July 9 meeting: the Blue Sky Golf hearing resumes at 7:15 and a Chapter 61B notice hearing is to be scheduled after town counsel review.
July 16 meeting: Select Board goals for FY2025 are to be discussed.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The ten votes the official minutes record all match ours in substance and outcome, but ours records two more votes (the Blue Sky Golf continuation and the Renee Emy nomination) that the official minutes never mention. The other differences are the date of the goals discussion (July 16 meeting versus a late-July workshop), decisions each record has and the other lacks, and the dollar figures. Those figures are heard only in the recording, because the official minutes print no amounts.
